_metadata.rubric: x04 rubric (natural-click standard + five content questions), 2026-10-19
_metadata.independence: I read only the instructions file and the single input file x04b-rd-input.json; no other file, repository search, web or paid API was used.

hints.reason: BALL via the disco ball and DANCE via disco dancing on the dance floor; an instant, fair click even if a little plain.

pairs.pair_note: Clean and easy; BALL could also read as a formal dance, but DISCO resolves both sides cleanly.

hints.reason: BALL via the disco ball and FEVER via Saturday Night Fever (and 'disco fever'); the pop-culture side gives a nice 'oh' moment.

pairs.pair_note: Good pop-culture pairing; FEVER is the fun side.

hints.reason: BALL via the disco ball and MIRROR via the mirrored tiles of that same ball (a 'mirror ball'); one object, instant click.

pairs.pair_note: Both sides route through the single object, so it is easy rather than clever, but fair.

hints.reason: BEACH via the Jaws movie's beach panic and BITE via jaws chomping (and the shark's bite); fair and quick.

pairs.pair_note: BITE works on both the anatomy and movie readings, which makes it very solid.

hints.reason: BEACH via the Jaws shark movie and BOND via Jaws, Richard Kiel's steel-toothed henchman; a great double reference for most adults, though younger players may not know the Bond character.
hints.fix: Jaws is the steel-toothed henchman from the James Bond films.

pairs.pair_note: Highest-delight JAWS pairing but the Bond side is 1970s pop culture; Jaws is a henchman rather than the main villain, hence the text fix. Worth a second opinion on recognizability.

hints.reason: BEACH via the Jaws movie and MOUTH via the anatomical jaws; a genuine double meaning that clicks quickly.

pairs.pair_note: Nice movie-versus-anatomy split.

hints.reason: BEACH via the Amity Island beach scenes of Jaws and SHARK via the film's great white; very easy, very fair.

pairs.pair_note: The obvious hint for this pair, and a good one.

hints.reason: BITE via jaws clamping shut and SHARK via the Jaws movie; immediate click.

pairs.pair_note: Easy; BITE and SHARK already sit close together, so delight is modest.

hints.reason: CINDERELLA via her midnight deadline and CLOCK via the clock striking twelve in that same scene; instant.

pairs.pair_note: The clock striking midnight is itself the Cinderella scene, so this is easy and fair.

hints.reason: CINDERELLA via the stroke-of-midnight deadline and NEW YEAR via the midnight countdown; two unrelated famous midnights make a satisfying click.

pairs.pair_note: One of the best in the batch: distant targets, one shared moment.

hints.reason: CINDERELLA via her midnight deadline and SNACK via the familiar 'midnight snack'; an odd couple that clicks neatly.

pairs.pair_note: SNACK side is a phrase join, but an instantly familiar one, and the pairing is fun.

hints.reason: CLOCK via the clock striking twelve and PUMPKIN via the coach turning back into a pumpkin at midnight; a Cinderella scene built from two props.

pairs.pair_note: Good scene-building; the player assembles Cinderella without her name on the board.

hints.reason: CLOCK via the clock striking midnight and SNACK via 'midnight snack'; both are instantly familiar, though the click is plain.

pairs.pair_note: Acceptable but one of the flatter MIDNIGHT pairings; CLOCK points at many times of day.

hints.reason: COLOR via the rainbow's band of colors and GOLD via the pot of gold at the rainbow's end; easy and fair.
hints.fix: A rainbow spreads sunlight into a band of colors.

pairs.pair_note: Fine; 'every color' is a slight literal overstatement (no brown, no pink), so a softer line is suggested.

hints.reason: COLOR via the rainbow's colors and LEPRECHAUN via his pot of gold at the end of the rainbow; quick and fair.
hints.fix: A rainbow spreads sunlight into a band of colors.

pairs.pair_note: Solid; same 'every color' softening as the other COLOR pairs.

hints.reason: COLOR via the rainbow's colors and UNICORN via the ubiquitous rainbow-unicorn imagery; familiar to a broad audience.
hints.fix: A rainbow spreads sunlight into a band of colors.

pairs.pair_note: Unicorn-rainbow is pop imagery rather than legend, but it is everywhere, so it clicks.

hints.reason: DANCE via disco dancing and FEVER via Saturday Night Fever / 'disco fever'; easy.

pairs.pair_note: 'Dance fever' is itself a phrase, so the pair is close, but DISCO is the natural umbrella.

hints.reason: DANCE via the disco dance floor and MIRROR via the mirrored disco ball; a clear scene.

pairs.pair_note: MIRROR side needs one step (mirror ball) but it is a familiar step.

hints.reason: EGG via its shell and TACO via the crunchy taco shell; a quick, fair food pairing.
hints.fix: An egg has a shell, and a crunchy taco comes in a shell (TACO line: 'A crunchy taco comes in a shell.').

pairs.pair_note: Idea is fine; the explanation and TACO line are sentence fragments and should be rewritten.

hints.reason: FEVER via Saturday Night Fever and MIRROR via the mirrored disco ball; both sides need one step, but both steps are familiar.

pairs.pair_note: A little more thought than the BALL pairs, but the click is real.

hints.reason: GAS via the Shell gas-station brand and MARIO via the Koopa shells thrown in Mario Kart; two unrelated worlds meeting on one word.

pairs.pair_note: A fun double meaning; Mario Kart shells (red/green/blue) are widely known.

hints.reason: GAS via the Shell station brand and NUT via its hard shell; fair double meaning, mildly satisfying.

pairs.pair_note: Fine but less playful than the MARIO or TACO pairings with GAS.

hints.reason: GAS via the Shell station brand and TACO via the taco shell; a pleasingly unlikely double meaning (and a road-trip scene of gas station plus taco stop).
hints.fix: Shell is a gas station brand, and a crunchy taco comes in a shell.

pairs.pair_note: Good; fix the fragmentary taco wording.

hints.reason: GOLD and LEPRECHAUN both via the pot of gold at the end of the rainbow; easy, though both sides travel the same single route.
hints.fix: A leprechaun guards a pot of gold at the end of the rainbow, and that pot is full of gold coins.

pairs.pair_note: The explanation repeats the same sentence for both words; it reads awkwardly and should be varied. GOLD and LEPRECHAUN are already closely linked, so RAINBOW is easy rather than clever.

hints.reason: GOLD via the pot of gold at the rainbow's end and LIGHT via sunlight split into colors; accurate and fair, at least as clear as the served HALO.

pairs.pair_note: RAINBOW and the served HALO can both stand; RAINBOW's LIGHT side is a real physical fact.

hints.reason: GOLD via the pot of gold at the rainbow's end and UNICORN via rainbow-unicorn pop imagery; pleasant and fair.

pairs.pair_note: Two fantasy touchpoints of the rainbow; works.

hints.reason: ICE via walruses hauling out on Arctic ice and MOUSTACHE via the visual 'walrus mustache'; the visual analogy lands with a smile.

pairs.pair_note: Exactly the visual-analogy style the owner asked for.

hints.reason: IVORY via the walrus's ivory tusks and SEAL via the walrus as a seal-like pinniped; accurate and reachable.

pairs.pair_note: IVORY will pull many players toward ELEPHANT first, but tusks plus SEAL resolves to WALRUS fairly.

hints.reason: LEPRECHAUN via his pot of gold at the rainbow's end and UNICORN via rainbow-unicorn imagery; two magical creatures meeting on the rainbow is a cheerful click.

pairs.pair_note: Best of the RAINBOW group: neither target is a plain property of rainbows.

hints.reason: MARIO via the Koopa shells of Mario Kart and NUT via its hard shell; fair, mildly fun.

pairs.pair_note: Works; NUT is the plain side.

hints.reason: MARIO via Mario Kart's thrown shells and TACO via the crunchy taco shell; a silly, satisfying collision of meanings.
hints.fix: Mario players fire turtle shells at each other in Mario Kart, and a crunchy taco comes in a shell.

pairs.pair_note: Fun; fix the taco fragment.

hints.reason: MIRROR via the mirrored disco ball is clear, but SUIT reaches DISCO only through Travolta's white suit or leisure suits, which most players will not think of from SUIT alone.

pairs.pair_note: The Travolta image is iconic once seen, but SUIT has many stronger associations (card suit, business suit, lawsuit); a reviewer who weights the Saturday Night Fever pose more heavily might pass it.

hints.reason: MOUSTACHE via the walrus mustache and POLAR via the walrus as an Arctic animal; POLAR leans to 'polar bear' first, but WALRUS is fair once MOUSTACHE is in view.

pairs.pair_note: POLAR side is softer than ICE or SEAL; passable because the MOUSTACHE side does the work.

hints.reason: MOUSTACHE via the walrus mustache and SEAL via the walrus as the seal's big tusked cousin; picturing a mustached seal gets you there with a grin.

pairs.pair_note: Strong: 'seal with a mustache' is practically a definition of a walrus.

hints.reason: MOUTH via anatomical jaws and SHARK via the Jaws movie (and the shark's own jaws); instant.

pairs.pair_note: Easy and fair; overlaps BEACH+MOUTH and BITE+SHARK in feel.

hints.reason: NEW YEAR via the midnight countdown and SNACK via 'midnight snack'; clean and familiar.

pairs.pair_note: Pleasant; less memorable than the Cinderella pairings.

hints.reason: SNACK via 'midnight snack' is instant, and PUMPKIN via the coach turning back into a pumpkin at midnight is a well-known idiom, though PUMPKIN first suggests Halloween or pie.

pairs.pair_note: PUMPKIN side needs the Cinderella step without Cinderella or CLOCK on the board; I lean PASS because 'turn into a pumpkin at midnight' is a common saying, but it is the weakest MIDNIGHT pair.

hints.reason: SEA via seashells (and the 'sells seashells by the seashore' tongue twister) and SNAIL via the shell it carries; easy and fair.

pairs.pair_note: SHELL is not contained in SEA, so the 'seashell' compound is acceptable.

hints.reason: SHARK via the Jaws movie and SWIMMING via the film's famous fear of going in the water; SWIMMING is the softer side but the movie premise carries it.

pairs.pair_note: 'Scared a generation out of swimming' is hyperbole but reads as a figure of speech, not a false fact.

hints.reason: TACO via the taco shell and TURTLE via its protective shell; instant and fair.
hints.fix: A crunchy taco comes in a shell, and a turtle hides in its shell.

pairs.pair_note: Easy; fix the taco fragment.
